white_space:
Caveat on confidence: my WebSearch budget (200 calls) was exhausted before I ran any query in this session. The verdict rests on direct fetches of about 20 competitor and source pages plus GitHub searches, not on a broad landscape scan. It is a provisional 'gap', not a confirmed one.

What I did not find: no company that ingests pharmacy-side remits, benchmarks per-drug, per-PBM reimbursement against a peer pool, models Q4 network offers, and ties pharmacy-paid amounts to an employer's PBM claims file. The employer-side audit market is served: Truveris, benefits consultants, and transparent PBMs that market pass-through. Their audits appear to start from what the PBM hands over, and I found no sign they hold the pharmacy-paid half.

The pharmacy-side gap is plausible. PioneerRx, PQS and CPESN pages show no reimbursement-benchmarking or contract-modeling feature. Not verified: pharmacy services administrative organizations (PSAOs such as Cardinal, AmerisourceBergen Elevate, AAP, Health Mart Atlas) and pharmacy management system vendors may already offer contract review or reimbursement reports to members. Confirm this in customer interviews before building, because the PSAOs negotiate PBM contracts and already hold members' remits.

The specific unserved wedge is a claim-level reconciliation between the pharmacy's actual paid amount and the employer's PBM claims file, delivered as a spread and rebate pass-through gap in dollars per member.

Risks that shrink the white space:
- PBM provider-manual confidentiality clauses and possible antitrust or information-exchange concerns when pooling competitors' reimbursement rates.
- Getting employer PBM claims files with sponsor consent.
- Pharmacy remits are not uniformly 835 files.
- The January 2027 contract window is roughly 3 months away and cannot be met by a product built from scratch.
evidence_of_demand:
Partial and mostly indirect. Nothing found this session shows pharmacies paying $99-199 a month for benchmarking, and no RFPs or forum threads.

Indirect evidence:
- FTC staff report (Jan 14, 2025) found the Big 3 PBMs reimbursed their own pharmacies more than unaffiliated ones for nearly every specialty generic analyzed, with $7.3B in excess dispensing revenue from 2017-2022. That supports the claim that pharmacy-side and employer-side ledgers diverge. https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/01/ftc-releases-second-interim-staff-report-prescription-drug-middlemen
- Employers and consultants already pay for PBM audits. Truveris sells audits and oversight and claims $7B in client savings. https://www.truveris.com
- Transparent PBMs are growing fast. AffirmedRx ranked #5 on the 2026 Inc. 5000, and Capital Rx is on the Inc. 5000 and Deloitte Fast 500. https://www.affirmedrx.com and https://www.cap-rx.com/
- Independent pharmacies are building their own underwater-Rx analytics. rx-gap-finder (July 2026) reads BestRx exports to find payer spread. https://github.com/ridham0065/rx-gap-finder
- Drug Channels (Aug 2026) ran 'The K-Shaped Pharmacy Shakeout: Consolidation in Cities, Lost Access in Rural America', which supports the closure-pressure premise. https://www.drugchannels.net

Not verified: the ERISA lawsuits, state PBM transparency laws and 2026 federal PBM reform cited in the idea's why_now. Two fetches for them (NCSL, KFF) failed.
sharper_angle:
Drop the two-sided marketplace at launch and start with one narrow, seasonal pharmacy-side product, then use it to acquire the employer-side data.

1. **Stay-or-leave modeler.** Sell it to state independent pharmacy associations and PSAOs as a member benefit, not to pharmacies one at a time. Process remits locally in the browser, as rx-gap-finder does, so the pharmacy keeps custody of its data. That defuses the confidentiality and antitrust objections. Pool only de-identified, aggregated, lagged benchmarks, and only with an attorney's sign-off. Check first that PSAOs and pharmacy management system vendors do not already do this.

2. **Claim-level tie-out, sold to buyers who can compel or pay for the data.**
   - Public plans: school districts, counties and state employee plans, where auditors, attorneys general and open-records rules can obtain PBM claims files.
   - ERISA plaintiff and fiduciary counsel.
   - Employer coalitions.

3. **Partner with the transparent PBMs** (Capital Rx, AffirmedRx, SmithRx) and consultants such as Truveris. Give them a 'verified pass-through' proof point built from pharmacy remits, which they cannot produce from their own data. Take a referral fee or per-audit fee rather than competing with their audits.

Before building, validate the first 15 pharmacies and one public-plan pilot for willingness to hand over remits. Confirm that a claim-level join between pharmacy remits and an employer PBM file is technically possible.
